comparison_source.citation: McBride, B. J., Zehe, M. J., and Gordon, S. (2002), NASA Glenn Coefficients for Calculating Thermodynamic Properties of Individual Species, NASA/TP-2002-211556.
comparison_source.source_locator: Appendix D, P4O10(L) card, printed p. 262; the liquid function cites Gurvich (1989), Part 1 p. 417 and Part 2 p. 270.
comparison_source.use: Phase-normalization comparison only. Divide Gf(P4O10(l)) by two for the P2O5(l) formula-unit standard; NASA's 1-atm pure-liquid standard still needs a pressure correction for a same-standard comparison.

standard_state: pure liquid P2O5; reaction gas reference pressure inferred as 1 atm from the assessment's metallurgical convention because the accessible equation does not state p°
accuracy: The 2012 article critically evaluates solid and liquid P2O5 data and derives liquid Gibbs energies from stable and metastable vapor-pressure data. The publication does not quantify a numeric uncertainty for this linear function.
source_note: Jung et al. (2013), citing Jung and Hudon (2012), prints log K = -16.92 at 1873 K, but the selected Delta G° equation implies log10 K = +16.92 for the stated formation reaction. The implementation uses the printed Gibbs equation and recomputes equilibrium constants from it. NASA Glenn lists P4O10(l), not P2O5(l); under the same elemental references and pure-liquid formula-unit standard, G°f(P4O10(l)) equals twice G°f(P2O5(l)), as derived in the builder comment. NASA's condensed standard is 1 atm, so the comparison needs a liquid pressure correction that is not applied without a molar volume.
